question: Suxamethonium (succinylcholine) causes sustained depolarisation of the motor end plate, resulting in fasciculations followed by flaccid paralysis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Unlike non-depolarising agents (which competitively block the receptor), suxamethonium binds and causes sustained depolarisation → fasciculations → flaccid paralysis until pseudocholinesterase hydrolyses it.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Suxamethonium mimics acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors but is not broken down by acetylcholinesterase, causing persistent depolarisation and flaccid paralysis after initial fasciculations.
